newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pertamina sets Mar 15 for Balongan CDU restart.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina sets Mar 15 for Balongan CDU restart.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned oil firm Pertamina has scheduled to restart its Balongan refinery in phases from March 15 after the refinery was shut on February 6 due to technical problems, a company source said on Tuesday.
The first unit to resume operations is its atmospheric residue hydrodesulphuriser, followed by the 125,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distilllation unit (CDU).
This will be followed by the 83,000-bpd long residue catalytic cracker (LRCC) on March 17.
The source said the LRCC, which produces gasoline, diesel and jet-kerosene fuel, will resume operations at 60-70 percent capacity.
Output will be raised gradually to 80-100 percent and eventually to 105 percent capacity to make up for loss production, he said.
The CDU was last shut on March 3 when the refinery residue tanks were full due to the LRCC's failure to process the heavier residues to lighter and more valuable oil products.
The problem started when one of the refinery's four functioning boilers malfunctioned and caused a leak.
Pertamina junior processing director Samto Utomo said on February 25 that attempts to restart the LRCC on February 20 failed because of what he described only as "another small problem."
